qs.q: Boric acid powder works as a cockroach control agent primarily through
o: Contact and stomach poison causing dehydration
qs.e: Boric acid acts as both a contact and stomach poison. It adheres to the cockroach's body, is ingested during grooming, and causes dehydration by damaging the exoskeleton and digestive system.

ai.subject: Microbiology & immunology
ai.summary: Cockroaches, especially Blattella germanica, are common indoor pests that can trigger IgE-mediated allergic reactions and carry enteric pathogens. Their exoskeletons and feces are major allergen sources, especially in low-resource settings.

sections.p: Blattella germanica thrives in warm, humid indoor environments and is a frequent contaminant in hospitals and food facilities. Its presence is a marker of poor hygiene and can exacerbate respiratory allergies.
The German cockroach is small, light brown, with two dark stripes on its pronotum. It reproduces rapidly, with females producing egg cases (oothecae) that release dozens of nymphs.

t.b: Presence of two dark stripes on pronotum confirms species

sections.p: Cockroaches spread allergens through shed skins and feces. They can mechanically transfer bacteria and viruses on their bodies and in their gut.

t.b: High counts indicate need for pest control

sections.p: Primary clinical impact is allergic disease: allergic rhinitis, asthma, and skin dermatitis. They can also carry enteric pathogens (E. coli, Salmonella) that cause foodborne illness.
Diagnosis is clinical, supported by allergen testing and environmental assessment. In low-resource settings, visual inspection and patient history are key.
Management focuses on allergen avoidance, environmental cleaning, and, if needed, pharmacotherapy. Treat underlying allergic disease with antihistamines or inhaled corticosteroids.

In low-resource settings, a history of frequent sneezing, wheezing, or skin rash after kitchen exposure should prompt consideration of cockroach allergy. Visual inspection of kitchens and patient homes can guide interventions.

faq.q: Can cockroaches cause infections in humans?
faq.a: Yes, they can mechanically transfer bacteria like Salmonella, but infections are uncommon compared to allergic reactions.

faq.q: What is the best way to reduce cockroach allergens in a home?
faq.a: Regular cleaning, sealing food, removing clutter, and using traps or baits to reduce population.
Not all species; Blattella germanica is the most common allergen source in indoor environments.
